newsitem.title: USA: BPA cuts Wed firm, peak power prices 50 cents/MWh.
newsitem.headline: BPA cuts Wed firm, peak power prices 50 cents/MWh.

text.p: The Bonneville Power Administration (BPA) cut Wednesday prices for firm on-peak power by 50 cents per megawatt hour (MWh) and raised the volume limit by 200 megawatts, the agency said Tuesday.
BPA offered up to 500 megawatts of firm power during peak demand hours at $12.00 per MWh for Northwest deliveries and $13.00 for California-Oregon border (COB) sales.
Wednesday firm off-peak power was offered at $9.00 for all deliveries, down from $9.50 for Monday and Tuesday.
Prices for non-firm power during peak hours (0800-1000, 1800-2000 PST) were cut by $2.00 per MWh to $14.00 (Northwest) and $15.00 (COB).
Non-firm prices for shoulder hours (0700, 1100-1700 and 2100-2200) were at $10.00 for Northwest and $11.00 for COB.
Non-firm prices for off-peak (0100-0500 and 2400 PST) hours on Wednesday were posted at $9.00 for all deliveries.
BPA also offered displacement power during off-peak hours on Wednesdasy at $7.00 per MWh.
